hook.line: Tomás keeps arriving late, and Vale has two ways to tell him. One is gentle and leaves room to joke. The other closes the door. Choosing wrongly turns a small complaint into a fight.
hook.es: Me molesta un poco que cierres tan tarde.
hook.en: It bothers me a little that you close so late.

examples.es: Me molesta un poco que hablen tan fuerte.
examples.en: It bothers me a little that they talk so loudly.

examples.es: Me molesta muchísimo que Simón grite.
examples.en: It bothers me a lot that Simón screams.
I can't stand it when people shout at me.
I can't stand it when people lie to me.
Does it bother you if I open the window? (to a friend)

examples.es: Me molesta bastante que no avisen.
examples.en: It bothers me quite a bit that they don't let us know.

rule:
Two ways to complain, and one has volume control.

*Me molesta* comes in sizes: *un poco*, *bastante*, *mucho*, *muchísimo*. It is good for small things and for polite questions: *¿te molesta que abra la ventana?*

*No soporto* is already at the top. There is no half of it, so never add *un poco*. It says: that is the limit.

Both are followed by *que* and a verb in the *-e* or *-a* form that you know from feelings: *hablen*, *griten*.
smallPrint: Teachers call this gradable versus non-gradable: *molestar* can be scaled, *no soportar* cannot.

options: It bothers me a little that they talk so loudly.
I can't stand that they talk so loudly.
It bothers me a little that people lie to me.

options: It bothers me a little that Simón screams.

I can't stand that Altamira is buying the block.

yourTurn.prompt: A little bothered. Fill the gap and type the sentence: ___ que hablen tan fuerte. (Me molesta un poco / No soporto)
yourTurn.answer: Me molesta un poco que hablen tan fuerte.

yourTurn.prompt: You can't take it. Fill the gap and type the sentence: ___ que me mientan. (Me molesta un poco / No soporto)
Say: It bothers me a lot that Simón screams.
yourTurn.answer: Me molesta muchísimo que Simón grite.
accept: Me molesta mucho que Simón grite.
yourTurn.why: *Muchísimo* turns the volume up, and *molesta* allows it.

yourTurn.prompt: Ask a friend: Do you mind if I open the window?
yourTurn.why: *Te molesta que* + the verb in its *-e* or *-a* form is the polite way to ask.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I can't stand it when they shout at me.
yourTurn.why: *No soporto que* + a verb in its *-e* or *-a* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it milder: No soporto que hablen tan fuerte.
yourTurn.answer: Me molesta un poco que hablen tan fuerte.
yourTurn.why: Only *molesta* can be turned down with *un poco*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it polite, to an older lady: ¿Te molesta que abra la ventana?

pitfalls.wrong: No soporto un poco que me griten.
pitfalls.right: Me molesta un poco que me griten.
pitfalls.why: Almost. *No soporto* has no size, so *un poco* doesn't fit; *molesta* does.

pitfalls.wrong: Me molesto que hablen tan fuerte.
pitfalls.right: Me molesta que hablen tan fuerte.
pitfalls.why: The thing that bothers you is the subject, like *gustar*: *me molesta*.
After *me molesta que*, the verb takes its *-e* form: *griten*.

personal: What bothers you a little, and what can you not stand? Say one of each: *me molesta un poco que...* and *no soporto que...*.
